title: When the Crown Wakes
premise: Oscar Joubert, a mercenary whose god Vael went silent years ago, has survived by staying small: guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains and asking no questions. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Oscar learns the map leads to the Hollow Court beneath Thornfell, where souls are sold as currency, and that his own sister's soul was among those sold when they were children. He gathers a found family of outcasts, a disgraced priestess, a debt-broken thief, and a talking crow that may be Vael's last fragment, to steal her back before the Court's centennial reckoning seals all bargains forever. In the end Oscar discovers his god went silent because it gave its voice to buy his sister's soul, and he must choose between reclaiming Vael's power for himself or spending it to free every soul in the Court; he chooses the latter, waking the crown of the mountain god at the cost of his own magic, and returns home mortal but no longer invisible.
about_author: S. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write character-driven fantasy about people the maps forgot.

chapters.title: The Silent God
chapters.summary: Oscar Joubert guides a smuggler caravan through a snowbound pass, praying to Vael out of habit and receiving nothing. A rival crew shadows them, and Oscar earns his pay with cold competence. The chapter establishes his isolation, his rules (never ask names, never take sides), and the hollow ache of unanswered prayer. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: weary self-sufficiency masking grief.

chapters.title: Blood on the Map
chapters.summary: A stranger stumbles into the waystation where Oscar winters, gut-wounded and raving about 'the Court beneath.' With his last breath the man presses a wax-sealed map into Oscar's hands and whispers a name: Joubert. Smugglers who saw the exchange come hunting. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: dread, as invisibility shatters.

chapters.title: What the Crow Knew
chapters.summary: Fleeing the waystation, Oscar is cornered in a ravine until a black crow speaks with Vael's cadence and drives off his attackers. The crow claims to be a fragment of the silent god and insists on coming along. Oscar wants to burn the map; instead he reads it and finds his childhood village marked. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: The Priestess of Ashes
chapters.summary: In the border town of Cinderhollow, Oscar seeks records of soul-sales and finds Sister Anwen, defrocked for preaching that the Hollow Court's bargains are theft. She recognizes the map's seal instantly. She offers her knowledge if he takes her with him. POV: Anwen. Emotional beat: bitter faith reigniting into purpose.

chapters.title: A Thief's Debt
chapters.summary: To forge Court credentials they need a forger: Pip Marrow, a young thief indentured to a crime lord after stealing to feed her siblings. Oscar wins her contract in a rigged card game he deliberately loses badly. Pip joins them furious and curious. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: resentment softening toward wary belonging.

chapters.title: The Village That Sold Its Children
chapters.summary: The map leads to Oscar's home village, abandoned since a famine winter twenty years ago. Anwen deciphers the truth: during the famine, desperate parents sold souls to the Court for grain, including Oscar's sister Lise. Oscar remembers being fed while she starved. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a drowned body.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Reckoning
chapters.summary: Court enforcers called the Tallymen ambush the group, seeking the map before the centennial reckoning locks all bargains permanently. The fight costs them their horses and nearly Pip's life. The crow saves them again, burning brighter each time. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: terror transforming into loyalty.

chapters.title: Road Beneath the World
chapters.summary: Anwen reveals a pilgrim tunnel into the mountain, sealed by the old church. They descend through caverns where sold souls flicker as pale lights in the stone. Oscar sees one light that answers when he calls Lise's name. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Names
chapters.summary: At the tunnel's gate, a stone warden demands a true name from each traveler. Anwen gives hers and loses her memories of her order; Pip lies and is scarred; Oscar refuses, and the crow pays in his stead, dimming badly. POV: Anwen. Emotional beat: sacrifice without certainty.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: They reach the Court: a vast cathedral-cavern where masked brokers trade soul-lanterns under a throne crowned with antlers. Posing as buyers, they witness a purchase that shows how bargains bind even after death. Oscar spots a lantern bearing his family name. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: horror wearing silk gloves.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: The chief broker, Lady Sereth, recognizes Oscar and offers him a deal: his sister's lantern free, in exchange for the map and the crow, which she identifies as stolen divine property. Oscar stalls. That night the crow confesses it made a bargain long ago too. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Lantern Light
chapters.summary: Pip picks their way into the lantern vault while Anwen, memoryless but instinctively devout, distracts the acolytes. Oscar holds Lise's lantern and hears her voice inside, still a child, still waiting. He cannot open it without a key held by the throne itself. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Price
chapters.summary: Sereth springs her trap: she never needed the map, only the crow, which she captures. Pip is caught in the vault and sentenced to have her own soul added to stock. Anwen's lost memories return in fragments revealing the church once served the Court willingly. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: betrayal and despair.

chapters.title: The Bargain Beneath
chapters.summary: Imprisoned, Oscar learns from a jailer-ghost the full history: Vael was the mountain's shepherd-god who went silent because it traded its own voice and divinity to buy back souls, one fragment at a time, hiding them in the crow. Lise's soul was bought with Vael's last coin. POV: Anwen. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: What Vael Gave
chapters.summary: The crow, caged beside Oscar, admits it has been gathering strength across chapters not to escape but to finish what Vael started. It offers Oscar a choice: take Vael's remaining power and become a god strong enough to break the Court alone, or give it up so the crow can unmake every bargain at the reckoning. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the weight of a god's trust.

chapters.title: The Centennial Reckoning
chapters.summary: On reckoning night, the Court assembles to seal all contracts forever. Sereth parades the captured crow and prepares to devour it. Oscar, Pip, and Anwen stage a desperate breakout using Pip's lockwork and Anwen's recovered rites. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: defiance against impossible odds.

chapters.title: Crown of Antlers
chapters.summary: Oscar reaches the throne and seizes the antlered crown, the key to all lanterns, but holding it means accepting the Court's power, becoming the next broker. Instead he uses it only to unlock Lise's lantern, refusing the throne. Sereth attacks. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: refusal as the story's moral hinge.

chapters.title: The God Who Woke
chapters.summary: Freed, the crow rises and unfolds into Vael's true form, waking the mountain itself. The climax erupts: Vael unmakes the Court's ledgers, Sereth is unmade with her contracts, and thousands of soul-lights stream homeward. Oscar holds Lise as she rematerializes, grown, remembering everything including his sacrifice. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: catharsis earned through loss.

chapters.title: Ledgers Unwritten
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, freed souls must find their way back to lives decades interrupted. Anwen chooses to stay and rebuild a honest church in the mountain's halls. Pip frees other indentured children using knowledge of the underworld she now owns. POV: Anwen. Emotional beat: bittersweet scattering of the found family.

chapters.title: Mortal Again
chapters.summary: Vael, restored, offers Oscar restoration of his mercenary gifts and a place at the god's side. Oscar declines: he wants to walk ordinary roads with his sister while she learns the world she missed. Vael gives him one gift anyway, silence that feels like company rather than absence. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: peace chosen over power.

chapters.title: The Long Road Home
chapters.summary: Oscar and Lise travel out of Thornfell together, taking the smuggler roads slowly, teaching each other who they've become. Pip writes from Cinderhollow; Anwen's beacon burns in the mountain. The crow, now small again, rides Oscar's shoulder by choice. POV: Lise. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: When the Crown Wakes
chapters.summary: Epilogue: seasons later, travelers report the Thornfell passes are safe, watched over by something antlered and kind. Oscar guides one last caravan, visible now, known by name, and finds he no longer minds. On the highest peak, dawn strikes the crown of the mountain like an answered prayer. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging.
